facts.fact_text: Some of the applications raise an issue concerning the right to freedom of peaceful assembly in connection with the applicants' protests against the landfill site near the town of Klin, Moscow Region.
In March 2018 the applicants started organising protests against the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
All the applicants except Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) were charged with various administrative offences in connection with their protests against the landfill site.
In November 2017 Mr Kotov submitted three notices of a public event (meeting) to the Klin municipal administration.
In May 2018 Mr Kotov submitted one notice of an environmental protest car rally to the Klin municipal administration.
Neither of Mr Kotov's applications to the Klin municipal administration for a public event or environmental protest car rally was approved.
All the applicants except Ms Kotova (application no. 106/19) were charged with various administrative offences in connection with their protests against the landfill site.
The details concerning the charges against the applicants, their arrest and the administrative sanctions imposed on them in connection with their protests are outlined in Appendix I of the judgment.
Neither of Mr Kotov's applications to the Klin municipal administration for a public event or environmental protest car rally was approved.
Mr Kotov brought a complaint against the Klin municipal authorities before the courts in connection with the non-approval of his applications for public events.
The details of the proceedings brought by Mr Kotov against the Klin municipal authorities are outlined in Appendix I (application no. 56764/18) of the judgment.
The right to a safe environment in Russia is contained in Article 42 of the Russian Constitution.

The right to bring civil or administrative proceedings by private persons or State bodies in respect of environmental damage in Russia is contained in Articles 1064 and 1065 of the Civil Code, Article 23.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, Articles 39 and 218 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, and Article 42 of the Land Code.

The obligation of physical or legal persons to comply with relevant environmental regulations in Russia is contained in Articles 1064 and 1065 of the Civil Code, Article 23.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, Articles 39 and 218 of the Code of Administrative Procedure, and Article 42 of the Land Code.
Articles 56 and 57 of the Russian Civil Procedure Code govern issues of presenting and collecting evidence in civil proceedings.

Ruling of the Russian Supreme Court no. 1 of 26 January 2010 contains detailed provisions concerning compensation of harm to life or health of physical persons and compensation for environmental damage.

Ruling of the Russian Supreme Court no. 49 of 30 November 2017 contains detailed provisions concerning compensation of harm to life or health of physical persons and compensation for environmental damage.
Federal Law no. 174-FZ of 23 November 1995 regulates environmental impact assessments for various industrial projects made by State bodies or public interest organisations in Russia.
Federal Law no. 89-FZ of 24 June 1998 regulates matters relating to industrial and household waste, including registration of landfills in the State landfill register, in Russia.
Federal Law no. 52-FZ of 12 March 1999 regulates the sanitary and epidemiological well-being of the population in Russia.
Federal Law no. 96-FZ of 4 May 1999 regulates air pollution, including the requirement of industrial self-monitoring, in Russia.

Federal Law no. 7-FZ of 10 January 2002 regulates the protection of the environment in Russia, covering types of polluting entities, the requirement of industrial self-monitoring, the right to information, the right to protest, the right to compensation, and the right to bring complaints.
Federal Law no. 99-FZ of 4 May 2011 regulates the licensing of activities of waste-processing operators in Russia.

Decree no. 322 of 30 June 2004 and State Decree no. 476 of 5 June 2013 (as in force before 30 June 2021) regulate the Federal Consumer Protection Authority's supervisory and preventative functions in the environmental sphere, including dealing with complaints about unfavourable environmental conditions, in Russia.
Sanitary Regulations 2.2.1/2.1.1.1200-03 of 25 September 2007 regulate environmental protection zones around polluting enterprises in Russia.
The applicants alleged that the large numbers of scavenging birds at the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry had threatened air safety in the area.
A military airbase known as Klin-5 was situated within 3 km of the landfill site at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

Representatives of the Ministry of Defence had requested the regional government of Moscow Region to have Aleksinskiy Quarry closed because its use had endangered the safety of military planes from Klin-5 airbase during their flights, owing to the circulation of birds above the quarry.

The authorities stated in reply to the Ministry of Defence's request that there were no grounds to close Aleksinskiy Quarry since the modern waste processing plant would be installed by 2021 and the quarry would no longer pose a danger to aircraft.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region highlighted the deteriorating environmental situation in Moscow Region and the need to implement modern waste processing technologies.

In a letter of 10 April 2013 addressed to the Russian President, the regional governor of Moscow Region requested the President to order the closure of twenty-four landfills in Moscow Region owing to their excessive storage capacity and obsolete technical characteristics.

In 2017 and 2018 State laboratories of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of Moscow Region and of the State Fire and Rescue Service and Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring carried out air quality tests in the vicinity of Aleksinskiy Quarry and in Klin.
From December 2018 to November 2019 a public interest group carried out measurements of air quality in the vicinity of Aleksinskiy Quarry and in Klin, using special testing equipment.

Excerpts from air testing reports produced by State laboratories indicate a number of instances where the maximum permitted levels (MPL) in the atmospheric air of Klin and its districts had been exceeded.
On other dates, air quality measurements in Klin and its districts indicated no excess of the maximum permitted levels (MPL).

A report of the state laboratory dated 15 March 2018 of air sampling in some of the villages near Aleksinskiy Quarry stated that a foul odour typical for landfills had been smelled in the village of Novotschapovo.
The state laboratory report dated 15 March 2018 stated that residents of the village of Novotschapovo should complain to the relevant authorities about the foul odour.

A notice of violation issued to Kombinat LLC by the Moscow Regional Department of the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment on 17 May 2018 stated that Aleksinskiy Quarry had exceeded its storage capacity by three times, with 833,186.20 tonnes of waste deposited in 2017 instead of an anticipated 270,000 tonnes.

According to a letter dated 16 July 2018 from the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring, the level of pollution in Klin had been classified as 'high', mostly owing to an overconcentration of formaldehyde in the atmospheric air.

The letter dated 16 July 2018 from the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring stated that the high concentration of formaldehyde in June 2018 in Klin could be explained by a certain type of repair works carried out at the time, solar radiation or certain chemical reactions.

According to an expert report dated 22 August 2019 concerning the project for a sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry, 1,662,625 tonnes of waste had been deposited at Aleksinskiy Quarry between mid-2017 and mid-2019.
The applicants submitted that the 1,662,625 tonnes of waste deposited at Aleksinskiy Quarry between mid-2017 and mid-2019 had been almost three times above the authorised limit for waste disposal.

A forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 submitted by Mr P. in reply to questions of the Klin Town Court concluded that the source of the 'foul landfill odour' could only have been the body of the landfill itself at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry was the only place in the vicinity of Klin that attracted large numbers of birds.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the violation by Kombinat LLC of sanitary, epidemiological and environmental regulations had resulted in detectable consequences for the environment and the health of the population.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the massive uncontrolled leakage of toxic organic waste (leachate) from Aleksinskiy Quarry had been practically impossible to remediate and had posed a real danger to the life and health of the population.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that the leachate from Aleksinskiy Quarry had seriously endangered the environment, had impaired the quality of fresh water and groundwater, and could contaminate soil and water sources for decades.

The forensic expert report dated 31 July 2019 by Mr P. concluded that Kombinat LLC had deposited waste beyond the established boundaries of the landfill at Aleksinskiy Quarry and had exceeded the landfill's authorised capacity for waste disposal.

In the opinion of forensic expert Mr P. in his report dated 31 July 2019, Kombinat LLC should have been ordered to take measures to prevent further breaches and to repair the damage caused at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

The Government submitted that within the framework of the 2018 Russia-wide 'Ecology' project, plans had been drawn up for the construction of a large-scale multi-level solid waste recycling and processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
The waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been planned to carry out the sorting and subsequent recycling of solid waste to help improve the environmental situation in the area.
The processing capacity of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been estimated at between 150,000 and 300,000 tonnes of solid waste per year.

The waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been designed to use the best available national and international technologies aimed at reducing landfill, lowering the risks of gas formation and foul odours and creating recycled fuels.
Kombinat LLC's project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been examined at a public hearing.
Kombinat LLC's project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been submitted for a State environmental impact assessment.

On 23 September 2019 the project for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been approved for implementation by the Ministry of Natural Resources and the Environment.
On 22 August 2019 the project for delimiting a 1.5 km sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been studied by the relevant State expert commission.

On 23 October 2019 the project for delimiting a 1.5 km sanitary protection zone around the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been approved by the Russian Consumer Protection Authority (CPA) as being in compliance with the relevant regulations.
The Government submitted that in 2019 the regional authorities of Moscow Region had approved an investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry for 2019-2027.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry had been in effect since 1 July 2019.

The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated the construction of systems for collecting and processing landfill gas, collecting leachates and purifying filters.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated the construction of a multi-level solid waste sorting and processing facility.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated sealing the body of the landfill and its borders to prevent leakage.
The investment programme for remediating and decontaminating Aleksinskiy Quarry stipulated collecting rainwater and diverting drainage.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for drainage and the treatment of rainwater at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for acoustic protection from birds at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for electronically controlling the amount of waste taken to Aleksinskiy Quarry by trucks to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC implemented technologies for collecting, decontaminating and disposing of landfill gas at Aleksinskiy Quarry to reduce the negative impact of its activities on the environment.
Kombinat LLC started constructing a reverse osmosis system for treating leachate at Aleksinskiy Quarry.
Kombinat LLC regularly (every three months) monitored emissions into the air, water and soil at Aleksinskiy Quarry and published the results of its inspections on the quarry's website.
Kombinat LLC complied with the judgment of 13 October 2017 of the Klin Town Court by paying the fine imposed on it in full.

Kombinat LLC carried out the relevant remedial measures for violations of the relevant sanitary regulations following the judgment of 13 October 2017 of the Klin Town Court, which had been confirmed by the supervisory State bodies.

The Government submitted that according to reports on atmospheric air, wastewater and groundwater quality testing carried out between 21 March 2018 and 10 June 2019 within and outside the boundaries of Aleksinskiy Quarry, the maximum permitted levels (MPL) of nitrogen dioxide, ammonia, carbon monoxide, phenol, xylol and toluene had not been exceeded.
The Government submitted that in 2018-2019 weekly air quality monitoring had been carried out in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry within 500 metres to 2 km.
Of the 1,206 air samples taken in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry, 1,170 were tested.

The air quality testing in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry indicated that the concentrations of hydrogen sulphide, ammonia, methane, methanethiol, sulphur dioxide and phenol had been within the relevant maximum permitted levels (MPL).
Water quality monitoring in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry had not revealed excessive concentrations of harmful substances.
Testing of groundwater from wells and boreholes and of soil in 2018-2019 in the municipal districts adjacent to Aleksinskiy Quarry showed no deviation from the relevant health standards.

On 31 January 2018, during an unannounced inspection by the authorities, concentrations of ammonia above the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL) had been detected at the air monitoring posts at Aleksinskiy Quarry.

As a result of the detection of ammonia above the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL) on 31 January 2018, Kombinat LLC had been ordered to take remedial measures in order to comply with the relevant MPL.

According to Kombinat LLC's letter of 31 January 2019 and supporting documents, Kombinat LLC had complied with the order to take remedial measures to bring ammonia levels within the relevant maximum permitted level (MPL).

The Government submitted that in 2018-2019 the authorities of Moscow Region had received seventy-three requests (обращения) concerning the operation of Aleksinskiy Quarry, including requests to have it closed.
The Government submitted that no complaints (жалобы) had been received by the authorities or regional medical organisations about the negative impact of Aleksinskiy Quarry on people's health.

Representatives of the Ministry of Defence had requested the regional government of Moscow Region to have Aleksinskiy Quarry closed because its use had endangered the safety of military planes from Klin-5 airbase during their flights, owing to the circulation of birds above the quarry.

The authorities stated in reply to the Ministry of Defence's request that there were no grounds to close Aleksinskiy Quarry since the modern waste processing plant would be installed by 2021 and the quarry would no longer pose a danger to aircraft.

Between 18 March 2016 and 29 April 2019 the regional and municipal authorities, including representatives of the Committee on the Environment of Moscow Region legislative authority, held eighteen public meetings in the form of hearings, assize legislative sessions and discussions in respect of operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry and its modernisation.

On 29 April 2019 a public hearing was held on the project for the construction of a waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry in order to obtain the views of residents, including those of the applicants, who provided their observations and objections on the issue.
Following the public hearing of 29 April 2019, the project documentation for the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry was sent for a State environmental impact assessment.

Information on air and water pollution as well as radiation in the Russian regions had been regularly published on the website of the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring and had been available to the applicants.
Information about the environmental conditions at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been published and updated by Kombinat LLC on its website.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region, during a meeting with residents of Klin and official representatives of Kombinat LLC, stated that the main complaint by residents was the smell emanating from Aleksinskiy Quarry.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region stated that waste disposal operations at Aleksinskiy Quarry had been carried out in violation of the applicable regulations.

On 28 January 2016 the Regional Minister of Natural Resources and the Environment of Moscow Region stated that the construction of the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry appeared to be the only solution to the environmental problems caused by the quarry.

According to a website dedicated to the national 'Ecology' project, the project includes nine environmental programmes, including a programme on waste management and waste processing infrastructure in Russia in 2019-2024.
The national 'Ecology' project's programme on waste management and waste processing infrastructure in Russia in 2019-2024 has a budget of RUB 450 billion.

The national 'Ecology' project's programme on waste management and waste processing infrastructure in Russia in 2019-2024 includes the introduction of recycling schemes and the construction of more than 200 waste processing plants in Russia.

According to information published on the official website of the Moscow regional government, a recycling system was launched in 2019 in Moscow Region to increase the reuse of materials and decrease the waste deposited in landfill.
Funds for the reclamation of landfill sites in Moscow Region were allocated for 2020-2022 in the regional budget.
A large-scale multi-level solid waste recycling and processing plant opened at the end of 2019 at the site of Aleksinskiy Quarry.
At the end of 2020 the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry started functioning at full processing capacity.

In early 2021 half of the solid waste collected at the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry was recycled, with 20% of recyclable materials (glass, paper, steel and plastic) recovered and 30% of solid waste composted.
In total, more than 100,000 tonnes of solid waste had been recycled at the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry, reducing the volume of waste disposal in the landfill by half.

Aleksinskiy Quarry closed in 2020 and degasification (burning of landfill biogases in a special high-temperature furnace) was being actively pursued to prevent the spreading of foul odours in the Klin District.
The construction of purification facilities at Aleksinskiy Quarry was underway following its closure in 2020.
Three more boreholes for the extraction of landfill gas at Aleksinskiy Quarry would be created in the near future following its closure in 2020.
A complex solid waste processing infrastructure has been under construction in Moscow Region since 2019.
Thirty-nine landfill sites in Moscow Region closed in 2020.
Ten modern waste processing plants have been launched in Moscow Region and 2.6 million tonnes of solid waste has been recycled by them.

The construction of four more thermal solid waste disposal plants in Moscow Region is planned for 2022-2023, with an estimated target of only 7% of solid waste being deposited in landfill, which is well above the target of the national 'Ecology' project.
In 2015 and 2016 the Klin District was named among the areas for which the highest proportion of unsatisfactory tests of water was reported.
In 2016 and 2020 the proportion of unsatisfactory tests of water from non-centralised sources in the Klin District was reported as compared to the average regional indicator.
Excessive concentrations of various chemical elements were detected in drinking water in the Klin District in 2015-2019.
The excessive amounts of iron and manganese in water in the Klin District had resulted in an increased risk of developing blood and immunity-related diseases.

According to the 2018 report, the higher proportion of unsatisfactory tests of atmospheric air in towns and villages in Moscow Region could be attributed to pollution from landfills where solid household waste was deposited.

In 2018 air quality testing was regularly carried out at landfill sites in Moscow Region, including at Aleksinskiy Quarry, where the concentrations of harmful substances were within the applicable limits that year.
In 2019 recycling schemes were being actively implemented in Moscow Region, which made it possible to deposit lower volumes of waste in the landfill sites.
As projected, the waste processing plant at Aleksinskiy Quarry started operations in 2019, where regular air quality testing continued to be carried out in 2019 and 2020.
In 2019 a technical station for removing iron from water was set up in Klin within the framework of the national 'Clean Water' project.
